newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech power consumption up 3.75 pct yr/yr - CEZ. [CORRECTED 15:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech power consumption up 3.75 pct yr/yr - CEZ. [CORRECTED 15:28 GMT]

text.p: Czech 1996 electricity consumption rose 3.75 percent, year-on-year, to a record 54,111 gigawatt hours (Gwh), but fell short of earlier forecasts, the main power producer CEZ a.s. said on Monday.
(Corrects all gigawatt hour (Gwh) figures in story to read in thousands).
CEZ said in a statement that household consumption led the increase, rising 7.5 percent, while large industrial customers' consumption rose just 0.5 percent over 1995.
"Above all, warm autumn weather and the stagnation in electricity demand in the industrial sector have influenced the decline in the growth rate," it said.
In 1995, overall consumption rose by 5.8 percent compared with 1994, to 52,155 Gwh.
Net consumption, or demand, excludes losses in the transmission of energy and power plants' own consumption. The figures are subject to revision, CEZ said.
CEZ, which has the second largest capitalisation of publicly traded Czech companies, has not yet released financial results for 1996.
The 1996 demand figure exceeded the previous record of 53,320 Gwh reached in 1989, the last year of communist central planning.

But forecasts by CEZ in July 1996 showed that the rise in demand would hit 6.1 percent for the whole year, accelerating from 5.5 percent in the first half, and reaching 55,100 to 55,300 Gwh for the full year.
CEZ said that the unusually high consumption in the first half was caused by the unusually cold and long winter.
CEZ spokesman Ladislav Kriz told Reuters the company had not fine-tuned its forecast for 1997, which currently sees demand increase "not above the 1996 level".
Forecasts made in the early 1990's, during the decline of heavy industrial production, anticipated that consumption would return to 1989 levels after the year 2000.
